findings.details: Sanitized Git probes omit the frozen safe.directory and core.autocrlf=true options. The exact probe fails with dubious ownership; with only safe.directory added it reports 91 false modified paths (3842 bytes), while core.autocrlf=true produces the required empty status. This blocks functional Cycle 1 before shard launch and can also reject package/CI repository identities.
findings.title: Pin canonical Windows Git options in every gate probe

findings.evidence: With GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=NUL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, the gate-style status command reports 12980 bytes on this otherwise clean detached Windows checkout; the validator-equivalent command with core.autocrlf=true reports zero.
findings.summary: Formal gate Git commands disable the user line-ending policy without pinning an equivalent core.autocrlf policy, so quick/package/functional CI can falsely classify the clean authority worktree as dirty before scientific execution.
